text.p: Bonds were expected to continue following Spain's lead with the spread between the 10-year cash bonds holding in the range of five to 10 basis points.
"The market came back from its highs as other peripheries took some profit. It is waiting for Spain to set the trend tomorrow," said one trader.
One trader said that he saw Spain well supported around current levels but without the strength to gain significantly.
The money market closed quiet but with some signs of tightening liquidity. Rates for up to 30 days were close to the Bank of Portugal's repo rate.
The escudo closed firm against the mark as the peseta also strengthened against the German currency. The escudo could make an attempt on the 102.00 to the mark level on Tuesday, traders said.
